answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token as collateral before it may post bids, then slash that deposit when independent, randomly assigned auditors confirm fraud. A harbor market might accept sable cargo claims only after checks against karst delivery records; copied identities still need separate deposits, so a sybil swarm ties up capital and risks losing it with every caught claim. This raises the attacker’s cost in proportion to the number of identities, while honest agents recover collateral after valid work.
